summary: The only runnable processes are the collector plus the offline CLIs (analytics, coverage, backup). Beyond M1-M4, four more live-flow links have no production caller: M5 approval-request send side (issue_one_time_token, format_approve, build_application have 0 src callers); M6 reconciler and health scheduling (compare/enter_safe_mode reached only from manager and drills; OrphanSweeper and all ops/health checks have 0 callers); M7 exchange-derived risk inputs (ConstraintSnapshot built only from fixture dicts; exchange_info() uncalled; no daily_loss or open_algo_count producer); M8 persistence (F-202).
expected: A composition root, or one process per runtime role, wiring signal->plan->notify->approve->execute->protect->reconcile->journal.
actual: Only data collection and offline analytics run. The execution, enablement, paper supervisor and loop, reconcile, ops health and drills modules and the Telegram app builder are reachable only from tests.
impact: No live or paper flow can run. Fixing M1-M4 alone still leaves no approval sender, no reconciler loop and no exchange-derived risk inputs.
evidence: __main__ only at collector.py:942, analytics/cli.py:758, coverage.py:609, backup.py:611 and scripts/. No [project.scripts]. Only loop: collector.py:908. tokens.py:19, telegram_notify.py:211, telegram_callbacks.py:712, health.py:292-568, drills.py:449-840, sweeper.py:116: 0 src callers. ConstraintSnapshot( only at simulator.py:303 and loop.py:106. binance_usdm.py:660 exchange_info has no reachable caller.
why_tests_miss: All modules are unit-tested with fakes. No process-level smoke test exists.
recommendation: Plan a composition phase with named processes (approval sender, bot runner, execution service fed only by adapter reads, scheduled reconciler/sweeper/health tick, paper-soak runner), each with an end-to-end smoke test.
known_prior: KNOWN M1-M4, F-104, F-106, F-122, F-956 (this finding extends them)

summary: No operational persistence layer exists. All *_to_row mappers have 0 src callers. The approval lookup/save_atomic callables and every JournalLike.record are Protocols with no PostgreSQL implementation; the only concrete record() is the in-memory DrillLog. Meanwhile analytics_store reads signal/plan/approval/order/fill/position/journal tables that nothing writes.
expected: Lifecycle entities and the journal are written transactionally to PG. Approval consumption, dedup, SAFE_MODE and enablement are durable.
actual: Schema and mappers exist, but there is no write path. PG writers are only the collector, the uncalled metadata refresh, and the kill-gate append.
impact: Every durable-state safety fix (F-126, F-127, F-951, Corrected Rules 10/25/28) depends on a layer that does not exist. DB-based live analytics would always read empty tables.
evidence: mappers.py:47,99,161,209,280,326,374 have no src callers. telegram_callbacks.py:206-216,254-256 are bare Callable aliases. Protocol record() at enablement.py:43, safe_mode.py:79, sweeper.py:55, health.py:90, killgate.py:90. drills.py:225 DrillLog is in-memory. analytics_store.py:38-47 reads via *_from_row.
why_tests_miss: Mapper round-trip tests only. Live-PG variants are skipped without TEST_DATABASE_URL.
recommendation: Add async SQLAlchemy repositories: transactional save_atomic with a unique consumption constraint, plan-hash dedup, and persisted SAFE_MODE/enablement rows rehydrated at start.
known_prior: Related F-112, F-126, F-127, F-951, M3 (this finding is the root cause)

summary: execute_approved_plan re-runs evaluate_risk with caller-supplied placement-time state and places sized.quantity. It never compares that quantity with the approved, hashed plan. The plan's quantity fields come from a second, cost-free, unrounded formula (planner.py:444-448, 'quantity_after_rounding = suggested_quantity'), so they never equal the traded quantity.
expected: Size once via the risk pipeline and store the floored quantity in the hashed plan. At placement, revalidate reject-only; never re-size (Corrected Rule 22).
actual: The order quantity is whatever evaluate_risk returns at placement. It may differ from anything hashed or shown at approval. Plan quantity fields are mislabelled pseudo-rounded, cost-free numbers.
impact: Approval immutability is broken. The journal, analytics and approval message misreport exposure. Rising equity between plan and placement yields a larger order than the one approved.
evidence: planner.py:444-448; sizing.py:59-60 adds costs; manager.py:418 'verdict = evaluate_risk(**risk_kwargs)'; manager.py:487 'quantity: Decimal = sized.quantity'; _check_approval_authorizes_plan checks only hash, ids and expiry.
reproduction: Trace manager.py:418->487->509-518. No equality check against trade_plan.quantity_after_rounding exists in src/execution.
why_tests_miss: Tests build risk_kwargs from the same fixture as the plan.
recommendation: Store the final floored qty and realized_risk in the plan. At placement, reject when the recomputed qty differs or when risk > rate x equity x 1.05. Remove or rename the planner's pseudo-rounded fields.
known_prior: Root cause doc F-017; related F-015/P16, P11 (code fork is new)

summary: The R denominator differs by evidence kind. BACKTEST uses realized_risk = floored qty x risk_per_unit (simulator.py:853, quantization.py:110). LIVE uses plan.risk_budget = equity x rate before rounding and regardless of the filled qty (live_outcomes.py:238). Live |R| is systematically smaller (by 0-40%+ after the 60% utilization gate and partial fills).
expected: One R definition: net PnL / risk actually taken (floored filled qty x risk per unit) for all evidence kinds.
actual: Live R = PnL / allowed budget. Backtest R = PnL / realized risk.
impact: Backtest-vs-live/paper parity, R-based drawdown and streaks, and kill-gate evidence are biased: live losses look smaller.
evidence: simulator.py:853 realized_risk=sized.realized_risk; quantization.py:110 _mul(rounded, risk_per_unit); live_outcomes.py:238 'realized_risk: Decimal | None = plan.risk_budget'; both feed stats.r_value (stats.py:48).
reproduction: allowed_risk 10, realized_risk 7, pnl -7: backtest R=-1.0, live R=-0.7.
why_tests_miss: Each normalizer is tested only with its own fixtures. No cross-evidence parity test.
recommendation: Persist realized_risk on the plan, scale it by filled/planned qty, use one field in every normalizer, and add a parity test.

summary: The no-blind-retry probes map only '-2011'/'UNKNOWN_ORDER' to not-found. GET order not-found is -2013 (A2 table), so the adapter re-raises and the manager returns ENTRY_STATE_UNKNOWN and enters SAFE_MODE. Every definitive entry rejection (for example -2019 or -4164) is treated as ambiguous and ends in SAFE_MODE, and the ENTRY_ABSENT branch cannot be reached. Protective legs probe query_algo_order first: if algo not-found is not -2011 (unverified), no SL can ever be confirmed, so every trade ends in SAFE_MODE plus an entry cancel.
expected: Classify errors: definitive 4xx rejection -> NO_TRADE without SAFE_MODE; each endpoint's documented not-found code -> absent; only timeout/5xx-unknown/network -> probe, then UNKNOWN.
actual: Every exchange rejection of an entry forces the in-memory SAFE_MODE. If the algo not-found code differs, live SL placement never confirms.
impact: Fails closed, so no money loss, but live trading is unavailable or stuck in SAFE_MODE after routine rejections, and operators learn to clear SAFE_MODE by habit.
evidence: binance_usdm.py:1212 and 863-866 match on the string '-2011'. The SDK BadRequestError str is '(code, msg)' (binance_common/utils.py:473-475). manager.py:183-196 treats any place_entry exception as ambiguous; manager.py:525 enters SAFE_MODE; manager.py:741-752 probes first. tests/test_execution_manager.py:715 uses '-2013 Order does not exist' as the probe-raises case.
reproduction: BadRequestError(error_message='Order does not exist.', status_code=-2013) through query_order_by_client re-raises; the manager returns ENTRY_STATE_UNKNOWN (test L710-727).
why_tests_miss: A fake adapter is used, and there are no recorded Binance not-found error fixtures.
recommendation: Verify the not-found codes for /fapi/v1/order and /fapi/v1/algoOrder, map on exc.status_code, and add a DefinitiveReject classification.
known_prior: Adapter comment flags -2013 as unverified; not previously reported

summary: The ExecutionAdapter Protocol declares place_entry/place_algo_protective as '**kwargs: Any'. Under mypy --strict the real BinanceUsdmAdapter is not assignable to it, and the hand-built entry and leg dicts are not checked statically.
expected: Protocol keyword-only signatures that mirror the adapter, so a composition root type-checks.
actual: A composition root needs cast or type: ignore. Key drift (for example adding good_till_date) is caught only at runtime.
impact: A runtime-only seam defect on the order path.
evidence: mypy probe tmp/architecture_code/proto/probe_protocols.py: 'Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "BinanceUsdmAdapter", variable has type "ExecutionAdapter")'. The SafeMode, sweeper and RestAdapterLike protocols conform.
recommendation: Give the Protocol explicit signatures and add a mypy-checked conformance assignment in a test.

summary: Tick rounding exists only on the live path, after sizing. evaluate_risk sizes and checks minNotional on the unrounded zone mid. The simulator fills at the unrounded mid and exits at the unrounded SL. Live then rounds the limit (never pay up) and rounds the SL toward the entry, whereas Corrected Rule 6 says round first and move the SL away from entry.
expected: One tick-rounded price set, computed before sizing and used identically on all paths, with the SL direction recorded.
actual: Live geometry differs from the sized and backtested geometry by up to 1 tick per price.
impact: Small per-trade drift: slightly more stop-outs than backtested, and the utilization and notional gates are judged on prices that are never placed.
evidence: gating.py:69-72,100-107; placement.py:199-210 'SL triggers round TOWARD the entry'; simulator.py:478-517 fills at entry_ref.
reproduction: Use an off-grid zone mid: the live limit differs from the simulated fill.
recommendation: Move price quantization into the shared core before sizing and fix the rounding direction per Corrected Rule 6.

summary: Duplicated logic and constants. placement.quantize_protective_qty re-implements risk.quantization: it applies MIN_NOTIONAL to reduce-only TP legs (Binance exempts them) and uses LOT_SIZE instead of MARKET_LOT_SIZE. The fixture parsers are copied functionally identically in simulator.py and loop.py. The live-5 universe literal appears in 4 places (backfill.py:549, manager.py:51, backtest/report.py:34, portfolio.py:30 cluster). MARK_PRICE, GTC and USDT are hard-coded literals.
expected: Each piece of logic exists once; universe, working type, TIF and quote asset come from registry or config.
actual: Copies can drift; the TP-leg rules already deviate from exchange rules.
impact: TP1 legs may be locally rejected when Binance would accept them; a universe change needs 4 edits.
evidence: placement.py:221-275 ('Mirrors src/risk/quantization.py'); simulator.py:60-325 vs loop.py:60-130; manager.py:515 GTC; manager.py:550 and placement.py:325,437,450 MARK_PRICE; live_outcomes.py:65 QUOTE_ASSET.
why_tests_miss: Each copy has its own fixtures.
recommendation: Reuse risk.quantization with reduce-only and MARKET_LOT_SIZE awareness; extract one parser module; centralize the constants in registry or config.
known_prior: F-908, F-958, F-056, P17 (duplication map new)

summary: src/domain/registry.py performs file I/O on REGISTRY_ROOT = Path(__file__).parents[2]/'params', and the Dockerfile does not copy params/, so any in-container backtest or analytics would fail closed with UnregisteredParameterSet. The uv base image is unpinned (:latest).
expected: Pure domain parsing; an I/O loader with an injectable root; the image includes the registry if it is ever used beyond the collector.
actual: Loading is coupled to the checkout layout; only the collector runs in the image today.
evidence: registry.py:41, 387; Dockerfile COPY lines copy src, scripts and alembic.ini only.
recommendation: Split the loader from the parser; COPY params if needed; pin the uv image digest.
